title: 1998 AHSME Problem 25
statement: A piece of graph paper is folded once so that \((0,2)\) is matched with \((4,0),\) and \((7,3)\) is matched with \((m,n).\) Find \(m+n.\)

solutions.text: The crease passes through \((2,1)\) with slope \(2,\) so it is \(y=2x-3.\) The perpendicular through \((7,3)\) has slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and meets the crease at \((\frac{19}{5},\frac{23}{5}).\) This intersection is the midpoint of \((7,3)\) and \((m,n),\) giving \(m=\frac{3}{5},\ n=\frac{31}{5}.\) Hence \(m+n=\frac{34}{5}=6.8,\) so B is correct.
hints: The crease is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining \((0,2)\) and \((4,0)\)
Find the line \(y=2x-3\), then reflect \((7,3)\) across it
